messages:
From: Priya Sharma <priya@novacorp.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: GPU SKU mix + canary routing plan for NovaCorp reserved commit

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking this. We’re finalizing an internal reserved-commit for Redwood and want a prescriptive recommendation for GPU SKU mix + a canary routing plan so our infra team can sign off. I’ve attached a small traffic sample and a high-level preflight PDF (both attached).

High-level asks:
- SKU guidance (H100 vs A100 variants) for our mix of interactive chat (70% of traffic) and reranking/embedding batch jobs (30%).
- Canary routing approach for initial rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and how to handle fallback when a cheaper SKU is transiently saturated.
- Any quick optimizations we should enable on day one (quantization profile, KV cache settings, batching targets).

Attached: novacorp_traffic_sample.csv, preflight answers (coming separately).

We’d like a short proposal by Sep 3 so our procurement cycle can include it. Is that timeline reasonable?

Best,
Priya Sharma
Director, Platform Engineering
NovaCorp

From: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Sharma <priya@novacorp.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: GPU SKU mix + canary routing plan for NovaCorp reserved commit

Hi Priya — thanks for the data, this is helpful. Timeline Sep 3 is tight but doable for an internal recommendation + canary plan. Quick clarifying questions so we scope the proposal appropriately: 

1) Concurrency profile: is the 70% interactive traffic mostly single-turn prompts or multi-turn chat sessions? If multi-turn, average session length (minutes) and average messages per session helps.
2) Prompt / response token distribution: can you confirm median and 95th percentile prompt length and response length?
3) Burst expectations: what does a P99 burst look like (qps relative to baseline)? Any scheduled batch windows?
4) SLOs: p50/p95/p99 latency targets for interactive calls. Tail latency budget is important for routing decisions.
5) Cost preference: are you optimizing strictly for unit cost or prefer headroom for tail latency at higher cost?
6) KV cache usage: do you expect heavy KV reuse across requests (chat with context) or mainly stateless prompts?

If you can answer those by EOD Monday (Aug 31) I’ll draft recommendations and loop in Karthik for routing/canary specifics and Marissa for SKU cost tradeoffs. I’ll also sketch a fallback policy (route to H100 pool, then to A100/quantized variant) based on answers.

Proposed next steps:
- You answer clarifying bullets -> internal draft -> quick review call (30m) -> deliverable.

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Priya’s note and the traffic sample. Can you each review the quick asks below so I can synthesize a single recommendation? I’d like bullet answers by EOD Mon (Aug 31).

Marissa: please prepare a rough SKU-cost matrix for the following targets: 
- Steady-state: 12k qps interactive-equivalent
- Burst p99: +2.5x baseline for up to 90s
- Batch embeddings window: 2–3 hour nightly window, peak 6k simultaneous embedding jobs

Karthik: routing/canary ask: propose a canary ramp (percent steps and duration) and an automated fallback policy for transient H100 saturation. Also include throttling thresholds and warm-up strategies (prefix cache seeding, pre-warming).

My initial hypothesis (untuned): 60% H100-80GB, 30% A100-40GB, 10% quantized T4-style pool for low-cost LLAMA-like workloads. Canary: 10% -> 25% -> 50% over 24–48 hour windows with automated rollback on p99 > 2x target. But I want your inputs before sending this to Priya.

Thanks — Jonas

Thanks, team — answers below and I attached our completed preflight PDF and the raw CSV sample.

1) Concurrency profile:
- ~70% interactive is multi-turn chat. Average session length: 3.1 minutes. Average utterances per session: 4. Median concurrent sessions during steady-state: ~1,800 (maps to ~12k qps interactive-equivalent under our prompt lengths).
2) Token distribution:
- Prompts: median 45 tokens, p95 320 tokens.
- Responses: median 120 tokens, p95 640 tokens.
3) Burst characteristics:
- Typical baseline: 12k interactive-equivalent qps. P99 bursts ≈ 2.2–2.8x for ~60–120s during product launches.
- We have a scheduled nightly batch window for embeddings between 01:00–03:30 UTC (2–3 hours).
4) SLOs:
- Target p50: 30–40ms per token; p95: <200ms per token; p99: <600ms per token for interactive paths. Batch can be relaxed.
5) Cost preference:
- Balanced. We prefer predictable tail latency for user-facing flows; willing to pay a 10–20% premium for headroom.
6) KV cache usage:
- Heavy reuse across chat sessions (context windows 8–32k). Cache hit ratio approx 65% from current telemetry.

Attachments: [Attachment: novacorp_preflight_answers.pdf (PDF, 124KB)] [Attachment: novacorp_traffic_sample.csv (CSV, 480KB)]

Let us know if you need additional telemetry (token histograms by route, per-region splits).

—Priya
Priya Sharma
Director, Platform Engineering, NovaCorp

Priya — thanks for the fast follow. Based on your answers we’ll deliver a short prescriptive pack (1–2 pages) plus an operational canary YAML for your infra team. Highlights from our internal draft: 

- Recommended SKU mix (initial): 55% H100-80GB (interactive-heavy), 30% A100-40GB (mixed workloads + embeddings), 15% quantized GPU pool (cost-tier for opportunistic/low-latency tolerable flows).
- Canary ramp: 8% -> 20% -> 40% -> 100% over ~36 hours (12h each for first three steps) with automated rollback if p99 token latency > 1.8x target for 10 minutes.
- Fallback policy: route to warmed A100 pool, then to quantized pool; tag requests by route and priority — premium routes never go to quantized pool.
- Day-one toggles: enable KV prefix caching, target batching 8–16 tokens for interactive with adaptive batching threshold, enable fp16 quantization for non-sensitive models.
- Cost/backstop: Marissa will include a cost-sensitivity table for a 10/20/30% headroom.

Action items:
- I’ll upload the canary YAML (draft) and a one-page recommendation doc to the Drive link and share with your infra team.
- Schedule a 30-minute review for Sep 4 at 10:00 PT — does that work for you?
- Marissa will attach the SKU-cost matrix; Karthik will attach routing thresholds and the rollout playbook.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood_canary-routing-draft.yaml (YAML, 4KB)]

If that timeline works I’ll prepare the HubSpot quote and the reserved commit draft for procurement.

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
